issues.legal_issue: Recognition for a teacher-training course cannot be made retrospectively effective to cover an academic session before formal recognition and affiliation were obtained.
material_facts: The institution applied for recognition for an earlier academic session, but the regulator later issued a letter of intent requiring further steps before formal recognition.
Formal recognition was issued for a later academic session and required the institution to obtain affiliation before admitting students.
The institution had not obtained affiliation when the High Court directed that recognition also cover the earlier academic session.
The High Court treated the delay and its earlier directions as grounds to extend recognition retrospectively.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not direct retrospective recognition; its order was set aside and the regulator’s order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 14 and 16 of the National Council for Teacher Education Act, 1993, and Regulations 5(5), 7(9), 7(11), and 8(12) of the 2009 Regulations, recognition follows satisfaction of the prescribed requirements and is distinct from affiliation; affiliation follows formal recognition, and admission follows affiliation. Recognition operates prospectively. The Court relied on Adarsh Shiksha Mahavidyalaya v. Subhash Rahangdale (2012) 2 SCC 425, including its conclusions that recognition operates prospectively and that an institution must obtain recognition and affiliation before admitting students, and on Chairman, Bhartia Education Society v. State of Himachal Pradesh (2011) 4 SCC 527, which explains that recognition and affiliation are separate requirements.

predicates.appeal_challenging_retroactive_recogniti: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a direction that recognition cover an earlier academic session.
predicates.formal_recognition_followed_required_ste: The regulator issued formal recognition only after the institution was required to complete further steps following a letter of intent.
predicates.affiliation_not_obtained_for_earlier_ses: The institution had not obtained affiliation for the earlier academic session when retrospective recognition was directed.
predicates.retrospective_recognition_unavailable: Recognition cannot be made effective for an academic session before the required formal recognition and affiliation.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges retrospective recognition and formal recognition followed required steps while affiliation for the earlier session was absent, retrospective recognition is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: Students admitted to a teacher-training course before the institution obtained formal recognition and affiliation are not entitled to appear in the examination, and regulatory delay does not validate those admissions.
material_facts: The institution admitted students without having obtained formal recognition and affiliation for the relevant session.
The institution argued that delay by the regulator had compelled it to admit students and sought permission for them to undertake examinations.
The Court found that the institution was required to know the law and could not admit students before obtaining recognition and affiliation.
issues.conclusion: The institution’s plea based on regulatory delay was rejected, and students admitted without recognition and affiliation were not entitled to appear in the examination.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 14 and 16 of the National Council for Teacher Education Act, 1993, and Regulation 8(12) of the 2009 Regulations require formal recognition and affiliation before admissions. In Adarsh Shiksha Mahavidyalaya v. Subhash Rahangdale (2012) 2 SCC 425, the Court held that institutions cannot admit students without recognition and affiliation and that students admitted by unrecognised or unaffiliated institutions are not entitled to appear in examinations. The Court also relied on A.P. Christian Medical Educational Society v. Government of A.P. (1986) 2 SCC 667, N.M. Nageshwaramma v. State of A.P. (1986 Supp SCC 166), State of T.N. v. St. Joseph Teachers Training Institute (1991) 3 SCC 87, State of Maharashtra v. Vikas Sahebrao Roundale (1992) 4 SCC 435, and St. John’s Teachers Training Institute (for Women) v. State of T.N. (1993) 3 SCC 595.

predicates.teacher_training_admissions_case: The proceeding concerns students admitted to a teacher-training course and their entitlement to take its examination.
predicates.students_admitted_before_formal_recognit: The institution admitted students before it obtained formal recognition for the course.
predicates.affiliation_absent: The institution had not obtained affiliation for the course when it admitted the students.
predicates.students_not_entitled_to_examination: Students admitted in those circumstances are not entitled to appear in the examination.

issues.definition: In a teacher-training admissions case, if students were admitted before formal recognition and affiliation was absent, those students are not entitled to appear in the examination.
